derivation.allocation: Six transaction reservations advance nextId/highWater to 7/6; capacity grows 1->2->4->8 and depth 0->3 before the first observation. IDs remain reserved while spawn commands are pending.
derivation.pendingSpawn: The first transaction stages six spawn commands and three relation commands, so pendingCount is 9; transaction FIFO executes spawns before relations at the barrier.
derivation.graph: Edges and inverse rows follow relation-graph append order: Parent 2->1, Parent 4->2, then ordinary Link 3->1. Approved linked cleanup removes hierarchy descendants 4,2,1 and then scoped owner 5, clearing the surviving ordinary Link.
derivation.owners: The component projection flattens first=[id] followed by second=[id+10,id+20], matching the approved #44 payload projection convention. Cleared slots become absent while the scope wrapper retains removed payloads in reverse clear order [5,1,2,4].
derivation.events: Each successful clear publishes ComponentRemoved as Removed:id before the record callback publishes Original:id; event history is retained through the repeated observation.
derivation.metadata: The frozen operation contract fixes resource=[77,88], registrations=[], nextSystemId=1, and clock=0. The observer scans 16 live positions, as in #44, while the component column has eight slots at depth 3.

assumptionsToReconcileWithConsumerDTO: The retained removed-owner projection is rendered as |removed=<flattened payload rows> immediately after the live owner slots.
The scope wrapper is rendered as the final |scopes=scene:id, list segment.
pendingCount includes all six spawn and three relation commands staged by the first transaction.
No registration or explicit clock advance is performed by the frozen pure setup/observation steps.
limitations: This is a finite six-entity, two-relation-family source oracle. It does not claim IO authority, Rust Drop behavior, foreign-world behavior, or runtime/compiler equivalence.
